source: Amirnet Tier 1 (A2, CEFR-J v1.5) headwords, data/amirnet-vocab.csv. Missing-from-bank list recomputed live by diffing every Tier 1 headword against every existing data/generated/batch-*.jsonl headword before writing. 20 alphabetical, single-word, unambiguous Tier 1 entries picking up right after 'cassette'..'chef' (the marker left by C-0545): cheque, chess, chimpanzee, chin, chirp, cleaner, clerk, click, climbing, clone, clown, clue, cola, comb, comic, composer, confused, container, continent, convenient.
selection_rule: Tier 1 (A2), skipping multi-word entries and headwords already present in the bank, alphabetical order, no skipping within the eligible single-word set. Next marker for the following tick (measured live after this batch): 'cooker'.
quota_rule: No per-batch ceiling (plan/25-content-commissions.md K-005, Roy 09/09; reconfirmed 12/09 — spotCheckPlan() runs per batch FILE, scripts/build-ingest-sql.mjs:159, not over the whole bank, so 1,200 rows is a per-file bound, not a per-tick quota — this tick's own scheduling prompt restated the same thing explicitly and named 12-row batches as an over-read of the old whole-bank ceiling). Batch size = 20, chosen deliberately: this tick opened by taking the lock and running `npm install` (no node_modules in a fresh clone; the pre-push hook refuses a push without it), which used real wall-clock time before content work could start. 20 rows is what could still be fully hand-checked against data/generated/allowed-words-2026-08-07.txt for every non-target token via a real gateSense run (not a sample, not an approximation), have every distractor read against its own three item stems for accidental validity (several — chess/king-queen, clue/hint, chin/body-part, container/hyponym — needed a second pass to narrow the stem so the distractor is actually wrong, not just absent from a list), and pass a 7-case negative control (one deliberately broken row per gate failure mode) before writing — all within one tick that also had to install dependencies and run all four generators plus verify. The bottleneck was per-item human care, not the pipeline; a larger batch would have meant lowering that care, which R-013/R-014 do not allow.
note: R-014 (replaced 10/09): no human sample-review queue; 16/20 rows carry translation_confidence = 'high', 4/20 (clone, clue, comic, convenient) carry 'medium' — clone (לשכפל also loosely used for photocopying, not only living things), clue (one_to_many with 'hint', both map to רמז), comic (קומי is the genre/register-precise word; מצחיק would be the looser everyday word — flagged for the register distinction), convenient (נוח also covers 'comfortable', see he_interference_note) — flagged rather than asserted, per policy. gateSense (lib/core/contentSchema.ts) ran directly against all 20 rows before writing, via a scratch validator script (.scratch/checkgate.mjs, not committed) that imports the real gateSense and the real data/generated/allowed-words-2026-08-07.txt: first pass was 2/20 (18 rows failed, overwhelmingly on level drift — an everyday supporting word not present in the NGSL-derived allowed-words surface-form list, e.g. 'zoo', 'scar', 'receipt', 'icon', plus two rows using a spelled-out number ('six', 'three', 'eight' — banned outright, not just a drift hit) and two using a proper noun ('Asia', 'Africa', also banned outright); every failing sentence was rewritten with an allowed-words-checked substitute (checked in bulk against the allowed-words file before rewriting, not by guessing) and a second pass ran 20/20 clean. A 7-item negative control (one deliberately broken row per failure mode: level drift, leaked answer, Latin letters in translation, fewer than 4 scorable distractors, missing blank, nikud in translation, headword missing from example), built on a passing row from this batch, ran through the same real gate: 0/7 passed, confirming the gate still discriminates. Distractor-in-stem placement (lessons 6/17/23/24 in plan/80-content-lessons.md) was checked by reading every item: four headwords needed a second look because a semantic-field distractor could otherwise have completed the stem as validly as the target — 'chess' (king/queen vs. checkers/cards, resolved by naming the king-and-queen pair and 'opening moves'), 'chin' (elbow/knee vs. other body parts, resolved with chin-specific actions — stroking, shaving-adjacent gestures — since 'shave'/'rub'/'scar' are themselves absent from allowed-words and had to be avoided), 'clue' (flagged with he_one_to_many_group rather than forced into false uniqueness against 'hint'), and 'container' (bottle/basket are literal hyponyms of container, resolved with a 'recycling'/'collect the waste' collocation rather than claimed as fully disambiguated — noted here as a residual, not hidden). ⚠️ OPEN FINDING, carried from C-0545 and unchanged by this tick: gateSense does not check distractor words against allowedWords at all (lib/core/contentSchema.ts read directly to confirm); distractors here were kept to simple, common A1/A2 English words by manual judgment, not checked against the old NGSL-derived allowed-words list, for the same reason C-0545 gave — that list was built for the old NGSL-headword era and the current headword source is CEFR-J (data/amirnet-vocab.csv). Still unresolved by PM/DEV; not decided unilaterally here. npm run build:ingest, npm run build:levels, npm run measure:gate and npm run build:preview all ran clean over the full bank after writing — see the commit for the exact row/file counts. No number is written as a word above 'one' and no proper name appears in any example or item stem (checked by the rewrite pass, not by eye alone, after the first gate round caught 'six'/'three'/'eight'/'Asia'/'Africa').
